title: Videos, season recaps and the competition calendar
summary: How to watch competition videos like a student, what season recaps show, and how the calendar helps you choose your first competition.

body.html: ClayArena has videos from Parcours de Chasse – Sporting™ and Compak® Sporting competitions, grouped by event. If you cannot travel to a competition, they let you see the sport up close. For a beginner they are also a free lesson in technique and rules.

Do not watch the videos like a film; watch like a student. Pick one shooter and follow them over several targets in a row. First look only at the feet and stance, then only at the gun, then only at the head and cheek.

Look for three points. The hold point is where the muzzles (the front ends of the barrels) wait while the shooter calls for the target. The pick-up point is where the eyes first see the target clearly. The break point is where the shooter plans to break it. Experienced shooters usually move between these points calmly and without hurry. More in Three points: pick-up, hold and break.
One more detail is the follow-through: after the shot the gun keeps moving along the target's line instead of stopping. If the video player lets you pause or slow a clip down, use it.
Look for the rules you already know as well. Seen in a real competition, they can be easier to remember.

html.sporting: Until the target appears, the top of the stock (the part of the gun that goes to the shoulder) stays below the line on the vest. Between stands the gun is carried open: a break-action gun is “broken”, with the barrels tipped down, so everyone can see that it is safe. Shooters, referees and anyone near the stand wear safety glasses and hearing protection.
html.compak: When a Compak® Sporting shooter calls for the target, the gun may already be at the shoulder or still lowered: the rules leave this free. So some shooters call with the gun already “mounted”, that is, at the shoulder. The shooter opens the gun before turning round on the station. Shooters and referees wear safety glasses; everyone nearby wears hearing protection.

body.html: Season recaps sum up a year: key championships, winners, rankings and notable results. Recaps of past seasons stay on the site too. They help you see who is in form, which events stand out and where you might go to watch live.

The competition calendar shows events with dates and venues. You can filter it by status (planned, ongoing or finished), by region and by month. You will find big international competitions there as well as events closer to home.

For a first competition, many coaches suggest an event nearby in a discipline you already shoot. Check the entry conditions, the shooting times and the dress code with the organiser in advance. How to enter: How to enter a competition. If the event is abroad, check the rules for taking a gun and cartridges there: Travelling with a gun inside the EU and Outside the EU: national permits.
After the competition, come back to ClayArena: your result will be in the results table, and the event may later appear in videos or in the season recap.

key_points.html: Watch videos like a student: one shooter and one detail at a time.
Look for the hold, pick-up and break points and the follow-through.
Season recaps sum up the year: key events, winners and rankings.
The calendar lists events with dates and venues and can be filtered.
Check entry conditions, shooting times and dress code with the organiser.

did_you_know.html: In Compak® Sporting a shooter has at most 10 seconds to call, counted from the shot at the previous station's target. In Sporting™ a shooter has at most 15 seconds between singles or between doubles. In both disciplines a shooter who takes longer first gets a warning from the referee.

quiz.explain: Watching piece by piece, one shooter at a time, teaches you the most.
